questions.question: A cube has flat faces. A sphere has ___ surfaces.
questions.explain: A sphere is round all the way around, so its surface is curved. A cube has flat faces you can put on a table.

questions.question: Can a sphere stack neatly on top of another sphere?
questions.explain: A sphere is round, so it rolls instead of staying still. That is why you cannot stack spheres on top of each other.

questions.question: Which object has only flat faces?
questions.explain: A cube has six flat faces. A sphere, cylinder, or cone all have at least one curved surface.

questions.question: You are stacking blocks to build a tower. A round ball rolls off the top. Why?
questions.explain: A ball is curved all around, so it cannot sit still on top. Flat faces are what let objects stack without rolling away.

questions.question: You want to stack two soup cans on a shelf. You can do it because the cans have ___ ends.
questions.explain: The flat top and bottom of a can let it sit still and stack. The curved side is what lets it roll instead.

questions.question: Your sister puts a ball on a slide at the park. The ball goes down fast. What does it do?
questions.explain: A ball has a curved surface, so it rolls down the slide. A flat object like a book would slide instead.

questions.question: You have 3 cubes and 2 spheres on your desk. How many can you stack?
questions.explain: The 3 cubes have flat faces, so they stack. The 2 spheres are curved and roll away. So 3 can be stacked.

questions.question: Look at a cube, a sphere, and a cylinder. How many have at least one flat face?
questions.explain: A cube has flat faces and a cylinder has two flat ends. A sphere has none. So 2 objects have at least one flat face.

questions.question: Maya says a cylinder has 3 flat faces. What is wrong?
questions.explain: A cylinder has 2 flat faces and 1 curved surface. Maya counted the curved side as if it were a flat face.

questions.question: Tom has a cube, a sphere, and a cylinder. He puts one on top of the cube. Which one can he put on top?
questions.explain: The cylinder has a flat bottom, so it sits on the cube. The sphere is curved and rolls right off.

questions.question: A cube has 6 faces. What are the faces of a cube like?
questions.explain: Every face of a cube is flat, so a cube has 6 flat faces and no curved ones. A curved surface, like the outside of a ball, is not a flat face.

questions.question: Ben gives a cube a little push on the floor. What does the cube do?
questions.explain: A cube rests on a flat face, so a push makes it slide. Round objects like balls and cans are the ones that roll.

questions.question: You build a tall tower out of cubes. Why do cubes stack so well?
questions.explain: A flat face sits still on another flat face, so cubes stack. A curved surface would tip or roll away instead of staying put.

questions.question: A cube and a can lie on a ramp. Which one rolls down?
questions.explain: The can has a curved side that touches the ramp, so it rolls. The cube has only flat faces, so it slides or stays still.

questions.question: Mia builds in the block corner. She wants her tower to stand up tall. Which blocks should she use?
questions.explain: Flat faces hold still on each other, so cubes make a steady tower. Round parts roll, so balls and tipped-over cans make the tower fall.

questions.question: Sam wants a block that slides down a ramp but does not roll. Which one should he pick?
questions.explain: Flat faces slide, so the cube is the right pick. Balls and cans have curved surfaces, so they roll down the ramp.

questions.question: Grandpa's rolling pin is round all along its long part. Why does it roll on the counter?
questions.explain: A curved side touches the counter at one small spot, so it rolls easily. Smooth is not the same as flat, so a curved side is not a flat face.

questions.question: At snack time Noah has a juice box, a cracker box, and an orange on the table. Which one can roll off?
questions.explain: The orange is curved all over, so it rolls off the table. Both boxes rest on flat faces, so they slide or stay put.
